BIRTHDAY GREETINGS 
 
MR. CHAIRMAN:  Hon. Members, I am pleased to extend  birthday greetings to hon. 
Members of Parliament, Shri Abdul Wahab, Shrimati S umitra Balmik, Shri Elamaram 
Kareem and Shri V. Vijayasai Reddy. 
 Shri Abdul Wahab, a three-time Member of this augu st House (2004, 2015 & 
2021), is a senior leader of Indian Union Muslim Le ague.  He is a dynamic 
entrepreneur and compassionate educationist.  He sp earheads several NGOs, with 
commendable credits, to their unwavering commitment  to service of humanity.  
UNESCO recognition to his vocational skill training  outfits is a tribute to his 
commitment and dedication. 
 Married to Shrimati Yasmine Wahab, the couple is b lessed with four sons-
Jabir, Javed, Ajmal and Afdal.  I wish hon. Member Shri Abdul Wahab a long and a 
happy life and extend greetings to his friends and family. 
 Shri Sumitra Balmik, a Member of this august House  since June 2022, is a 
grassroot politician, rising from Municipal Council lor to Parliamentarian, all through 
her dedication to welfare of downtrodden. Her four decades of political journey is 
marked with impressive accomplishments. Her very pr esence in this House is an 
acknowledgment of Bharat's commitment to honour "Na ri Shakti."  She is blessed 
with two daughters (Manisha and Mani) and a son Rup esh.  I wish her a long and 
healthy life and extend greetings to her family, friends and well-wishers. 
 Shri Elamaram Kareem, three-time Member of Kerala Legislative Assembly and 
former Minister in Kerala Government, is a Member o f this august House since July, 
2018.  From being a student activist, he contribute d significantly for five decades for 
the cause of trade unionism; has tirelessly champio ned the welfare of workers; and 
has been recognised for reviving the tile industry in Kerala.  He has also represented 
India's voice at various international forums, incl uding International Labour 
Organisation, Geneva.  Married to Shrimati Rahmath P.K., the couple has two 
Daughters-- Sumi and Nimi. 
 I join this august House in wishing Shri Kareem an d family a healthy and a 
happy life.  May the society at large continue to b enefit from his wisdom for years to 
come.   


 
 Shri V. Vijayasai Reddy - a second term Member of this august House, is a 
leader of the Y.S.R.C. Parliamentary Party in the Rajya Sabha. His vast knowledge 
and rich experience is aptly reflected in the contributions made in this House.   He, as 
Chairman, steered committee proceedings directionally and thoughtfully taking some 
innovative steps.  
A Chartered Accountant by profession, he has also served on the Board of 
Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams and as Director in public sector banks. Married to 
Shrimati Venumbaka Sunanda Reddy, the couple is blessed with daughter, V. Neha.  
Hon. Members, on behalf of this House, I wish him and his family, a long, 
healthy and happy life.  
  OBITUARY REFERENCES  MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, I refer with profound sorrow to the passing away of His Excellency Dr. Seyyed Ebrahim Raisi, President of the Islamic Republic of Iran; His Excellency Dr. Hossein Amir-Abdollahian, Foreign Minister of Islamic Republic of Iran; His Excellency Alhaj Ali Hassan Mwinyi, former President of the United Republic of Tanzania; and, His Excellency Dr. Saulos Klaus Chilima, Vice President of the Republic of Malawi.  Dr. Seyyed Ebrahim Raisi, President of the Islamic Republic of Iran and Dr. Hossein Amir-Abdollahian, Foreign Minister of Islamic Republic of Iran and other senior Iranian officials passed away in an unfortunate helicopter crash on 19th May, 2024. They will always be remembered for their efforts and contributions in strengthening our bilateral relationships.  On behalf of our country, I visited the Islamic Republic of Iran on 22nd May, 2024 and attended the official ceremony and personally paid tributes to the dignitaries. Our nation also observed a day of national mourning on 21st May, 2024.  His Excellency Alhaj Ali Hassan Mwinyi, passed away on 29th February, 2024 at Dar es Salaam. He was the second President of the United Republic of Tanzania from 1985 to 1995 and had implemented the economic recovery policy and steered Tanzania towards growth and prosperity. His liberal economic policies brought relief to the Indian diaspora in Tanzania involved in trade and businesses.  Our nation has deep appreciation and respect for his exemplary leadership and contribution in advancement of India-Tanzania relations.  Dr. Saulos Klaus Chilima passed away on the 10th June, 2024, when a Malawi Defence Force aircraft carrying him and nine others crashed while attempting to land.

Airtel Malawi. 
 The House joins the bereaved families, the Governm ent and people of the 
Islamic Republic of Iran, United Republic of Tanzan ia and Republic of Malawi in 
mourning the passing away of His Excellencies, Dr. Seyyed Ebrahim Raisi, Dr. 
Hossein Amir-Abdollahian, Alhaj Ali Hassan Mwinyi and Dr. Saulos Klaus Chilima. 
 I request hon. Members to rise in their places and  observe silence as a mark of 
respect to the memory of the departed.

REFERENCE BY THE CHAIR 
 
(i) Anniversary of blowing up of AI 182 Flight “Kanishka ” 
 
MR. CHAIRMAN:   Hon. Members, June 23 rd , 2024 marked the anniversary of one of 
the darkest days in the fight against terrorism.  T wo Air India aircraft flying out of 
Canada were targeted by terrorists.  329 innocent people lost their lives when Air India 
182 "Kanishka" was blown up off Ireland on June 23 rd , 1985.  Two others were killed 
as another major catastrophe was narrowly averted in Japan.   
Regrettably, justice was never fully served in thes e cases.  These incidents are 
a grim reminder of why the world must show zero tol erance towards terrorism and 
violent extremism.  Such acts can never be condoned  or justified or countenanced 
under any pretext.   
 
 
3
[1 July, 2024]


 
(ii) Kuwait Fire incident 
 
MR. CHAIRMAN:  Hon. Members, in a tragic fire accident that took place on 12 th 
June, 2024, in a residential building, a labour housing facility in Mangaf area of 
Kuwait, 49 persons, including 45 Indians, lost their lives and more than 50 persons 
got injured.  The loss of precious lives in this tragic incident is indeed painful and 
unfortunate.  Our Embassy in Kuwait, in coordination with the local authorities, 
ensured safe evacuation and necessary assistance to those injured from the accident 
site and immediate repatriation of the mortal remains of the deceased to our country.   
This House joins me in expressing heartfelt condolences as well as deep 
sympathy to the families of those who lost their lives and wishes early recovery of 
those injured.   
I request Members to rise in their places and observe silence as a mark of 
respect to the memory of those who lost their lives in these tragic incidents. 
(Hon. Members then stood in silence for one minute) 
  FELICITATIONS BY THE CHAIR  MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, Bharat, one-sixth of humanity, was elated by the spectacular victory by the Men in Blue in the T20 Cricket World Cup, on a glorious Saturday at Bridgetown in Barbados, as Team India defeated spirited South Africa in the final Match. Stupendous performance by our cricketers who remained undefeated throughout the tournament is testament to their dedication and hard work. It is a celebration of teamwork, resilience and relentless pursuit of excellence.  Hon. Members, as we rejoice this momentous glory, let us also remember that such historical accomplishments inspire every citizen of our nation to dream big, work hard and achieve eminence.  I would also like to congratulate the South African cricket team for their excellent performance who came very close to clinching their maiden trophy. Their heroic performance is praiseworthy.  Hon. Members, on my behalf and on behalf of this august House, I extend our heartiest congratulations to the cricketers, the management, the ground staff, the coach, the BCCI and everyone connected with the Indian Cricket Team. May they continue to scale new heights, bring laurels to the country and inspire the nation for greater glory in our Amrit Kaal.

endeavour of the Government to provide right opport unities to the youth of the 
country to demonstrate their talent. Whether it is competitive examinations or 
Government recruitment, there should be no reason f or any hindrance. This process 
requires complete transparency and probity. Regardi ng the recent instances of paper
